name: FEMA National Risk Index (NRI)
what_it_measures: Composite and per-hazard risk scores (18 natural hazards — flood, wildfire, heat wave, hurricane, earthquake, etc.) plus expected annual loss, social vulnerability, and community resilience components, for every US county and census tract.
coverage: national (all US counties and census tracts)
update_frequency: periodic (FEMA has released a handful of updated editions since the NRI's initial launch; not a continuously-updated time series)
history_available: An archive of prior NRI editions exists (hazards.fema.gov/nri/data-archive), but this is a slowly-revised structural risk score, not a long monthly/annual time series suited to the backtest's lead/lag correlation method.
access_method: Free direct bulk download — CSV/table, shapefile, and geodatabase formats — from FEMA's own site, no login, no key.
license: Data.gov lists the license as https://www.usa.gov/government-works (standard US government works notice — generally no copyright restriction), but a related FEMA/CRSI dataset on Data.gov is tagged with a different (EPA Science Hub) license, so the exact file's license should be re-checked against the metadata bundled with the specific download, not assumed from the dataset family.
fills_gap: backend/app/sources/livability.py's future_floodplain source is NYC-specific (NYC Open Data). The project's stated goal of generalizing to any US neighborhood currently has no hazard/climate-risk signal at all outside NYC. NRI would give every US county/tract a comparable multi-hazard risk score for the livability/risk pillar of the growth score.
caveats: This is a slowly-changing structural score, not a growth predictor in the backtest sense — don't expect meaningful correlation/lead-lag against FHFA HPI or Zillow ZORI; its value is as a risk-adjustment input, not a return predictor.
Re-confirm the license on the actual file metadata before implementing, given the conflicting license tag seen on a sibling FEMA dataset.

Tract-level is finer than the project's current NTA-level NYC geography; would need a tract->NTA (and, post area-model migration, tract->CBSA-area) crosswalk, similar to the existing ZIP->NTA weighting pattern in zillow_research.py.
recommendation_note: Free, nationally complete at a granularity the project can already crosswalk (same pattern as the existing ZIP->NTA weighting), and fills a concrete, currently NYC-only pillar. Primary open item is confirming the license on the specific download file, which add-data-source's ToS check should do before implementation.
